qualifications_or_emphasis: Standalone: Non-recognition of interest on financial assistance availed from July 01, 2024 onwards - loss before tax understated by Rs 884.96 lakhs for quarter and Rs 4,107.69 lakhs for year; current liabilities understated by Rs 7,027.26 lakhs as at March 31, 2026

Consolidated: Same as standalone plus GIPL non-recognition of interest from October 01, 2024 - loss before tax understated by Rs 361.22 lakhs for quarter and Rs 1,464.92 lakhs for year; current liabilities understated by Rs 2,195.39 lakhs

Consolidated: OSEPL recognized Rs 17,289.27 lakhs from NHAI on termination claims in Other Equity instead of Statement of Profit and Loss - loss overstated by Rs 17,289.27 lakhs for quarter and year; no impact on Other Equity
Emphasis of Matter and Key Audit Matters also provided in Auditors' Report
Material uncertainty relating to going concern due to defaults in repayment of dues and financial position

Basis for Qualified Opinion - Standalone: Company has not recognized interest on financial assistance availed from July 01, 2024 onwards, non-compliance with Ind AS 1 and Ind AS 109. Loss before tax for quarter ended March 31, 2026 understated by Rs 884.96 lakhs, profit before tax for year ended March 31, 2026 overstated by Rs 4,107.69 lakhs, current liabilities as at March 31, 2026 understated by Rs 7,027.26 lakhs.

Basis for Qualified Opinion - Consolidated: (i) Holding Company non-recognition of interest from July 01, 2024. (ii) GIPL non-recognition of interest from October 01, 2024. (iii) OSEPL recognition of NHAI compensation in Other Equity instead of P&L.
Emphasis of Matter and Key Audit Matters mentioned in Auditors' Report

Basis for Qualified Opinion: Company has not recognized interest on financial assistance availed from July 01, 2024 onwards, not in compliance with Ind AS 1 and Ind AS 109; profit before tax overstated by Rs 4,107.69 lakhs and current liabilities understated by Rs 7,027.26 lakhs

Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern: Company has defaulted in repayment of dues and incurred significant losses as at March 31, 2026, indicating material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt on ability to continue as a going concern

Emphasis of Matter: Termination of projects of KEPL and MTPL (associates); claims filed are sub judice; management considers carrying amount of investments and receivables reasonable and appropriate for recovery
Emphasis of Matter: Search proceedings under Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 at GIPL (subsidiary)

The Company has not recognized interest on the financial assistance availed from July 01, 2024 onwards which is not in compliance of Ind AS 1 'Presentation of Financial Statements' read with Ind AS 109 'Financial Instruments'. Due to this, loss before tax for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 has been understated by Rs 884.96 lakhs and profit before tax for the year ended March 31, 2026 has been overstated by Rs 4,107.69 lakhs and the current liabilities as at March 31, 2026 has been understated by Rs 7,027.26 lakhs.

The Company has defaulted in repayment of its dues. The Company has incurred significant losses as at March 31, 2026. These conditions, along with other matters, indicate the existence of a material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt on the Company's ability to continue as a going concern.

Material uncertainty related to Going Concern: The Holding Company has defaulted in repayment of its dues. The Holding Company has incurred significant losses as at March 31, 2026. These conditions, along with other matters, indicate the existence of a material uncertainty that may cast significant doubt on the Holding Company's ability to continue as a going concern.

Holding Company not recognized interest on financial assistance from July 1, 2024 (non-compliance with Ind AS 1 and Ind AS 109), understating loss before tax by Rs 4,107.69 lakhs and current liabilities by Rs 7,027.26 lakhs for year ended March 31, 2026

Subsidiary GIPL not recognized interest on financial assistance from October 1, 2024 (non-compliance with Ind AS 1 and Ind AS 109), understating loss before tax by Rs 1,464.92 lakhs and current liabilities by Rs 2,195.39 lakhs for year ended March 31, 2026

Subsidiary OSEPL recognized Rs 17,289.27 lakhs from NHAI termination compensation in Other Equity instead of Statement of Profit and Loss (non-compliance with Ind AS 109), overstating loss by same amount
Search proceedings under Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 at GIPL
Termination of projects of associates KEPL and MTPL with claims sub judice

outlook.statement: India's growth outlook remains favourable despite persistent global uncertainties. RBI projected real GDP growth of 6.6% in FY2026-27, supported by robust consumption, improving private investment, healthy corporate and banking sector balance sheets, and continued public capital expenditure. Geopolitical tensions, volatility in global energy prices, trade policy uncertainty and supply chain disruptions remain key downside risks.

India's roads and highways sector continues to offer significant investment opportunities, supported by Government's long-term vision for infrastructure-led growth. MoRTH identified a PPP project pipeline of 13,400 km with estimated cost of Rs 8.3 Lakh Crore over next three years. NHAI realized over Rs 28,300 Crore through InvIT and TOT models in FY2025-26. For FY2026-27, NHAI identified 17 highway assets spanning 1,692.5 km across nine states for monetisation through TOT and InvIT routes.

Sustained public investment, expanding PPP pipeline, greater private participation, asset monetisation and technology-led road management are expected to support the sector's growth. For experienced road infrastructure companies with capabilities across PPP projects, concession management, tolling, operations and asset lifecycle management, the evolving highway landscape is expected to create a wider spectrum of opportunities.

The Company has undertaken and continues to pursue various strategic initiatives aimed at strengthening its financial position and improving operational performance by leveraging technology to enhance toll operations, improve revenue collection efficiency and optimise operating costs.

The Company is strengthening its claims and litigation management framework with a view to expediting the adjudication and realization of outstanding claims. It is actively exploring mediation, conciliation and other alternative dispute resolution mechanisms for the amicable settlement of longstanding disputes.
